restoration_note: Three-parable riddle: First Man / Ship-with-Living-Spirit / Third Ambassador as one redemption in three discrete registers. The First Man parable (1597-1602) and the Living Spirit parable (1609-1615) are well-constrained by the recurring formulas (ⲣⲱⲙⲉ ⲛ̄ⲉⲡⲓⲥⲏⲙⲟⲥ — ⲡⲉϩⲭⲣⲏⲙⲁ — ⲛⲉϩⲱⲛⲏⲣⲉ — ⲥⲁⲧϩ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ⲍⲛ ⲛ̄ⲟⲓⲭ ⲛ̄ⲛⲉϩⲭⲁⲭⲉ — ⲣⲁⲓⲭⲙⲁⲗⲱⲧⲓⲍⲉ), so most editor restorations stand. The Ambassador parable (1617-1621), though clearly mirroring the same redemption-vocabulary (wealth, captives, powers of light, sons-with-soul, country of captivity), is too fragmentary in its connective syntax to support invented fills, so {32}{33}{34}{38}{39}{40}{41}{42} are honestly left unrestored. Local connective particles {16}{17}{21}{22}{23} are likewise too weakly constrained.
